builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
summary: Ambient SFT replaces standard supervised fine-tuning by adding a regularization objective requiring the fine-tuned model's high-temperature conditional distributions to match those of a frozen copy of the pre-trained model, with temperature interpolating between pure SFT (T to infinity) and full knowledge distillation (T = 1). The cost is a frozen reference model held in memory alongside the trainable model and additional logit computations per training step, comparable to standard distillation overhead, plus a temperature hyperparameter that must be tuned. It can fail if the pre-trained model's distribution is poorly calibrated for the target domain, if the temperature is mis-set (too high reverts to SFT's overfitting, too low propagates the teacher's noise), and the reported gains are relative improvements over SFT rather than absolute capability claims, so results may be marginal when the fine-tuning set is already large or diverse.
rationale: Ambient SFT is a low-cost modification of standard SFT that plausibly mitigates overfitting and forgetting on small datasets, but the 21% gain is an upper bound across benchmarks and should be validated on the reader's specific fine-tuning workload.
technique: Ambient SFT: temperature-matched teacher regularization for fine-tuning

claims.statement: Ambient SFT replaces standard supervised fine-tuning by adding a regularization objective requiring the fine-tuned model's high-temperature conditional distributions to match those of a frozen copy of the pre-trained model, with temperature interpolating between pure SFT (T to infinity) and full knowledge distillation (T = 1). The cost is a frozen reference model held in memory alongside the trainable model and additional logit computations per training step, comparable to standard distillation overhead, plus a temperature hyperparameter that must be tuned. It can fail if the pre-trained model's distribution is poorly calibrated for the target domain, if the temperature is mis-set (too high reverts to SFT's overfitting, too low propagates the teacher's noise), and the reported gains are relative improvements over SFT rather than absolute capability claims, so results may be marginal when the fine-tuning set is already large or diverse.
The authors report up to 21% average relative improvement over standard SFT across domain adaptation, instruction-tuning, and reasoning benchmarks.
